question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Six months from the date the employee was offered employment in the Institute: the officer or employee "may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [621/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- This applies to officers/employees of the National Building Research Organisation who opt out of employment in the new Institute [621/2025 §33(2)(a)–(b)].
- On opting out, compensation is paid under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [621/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The evidence is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-07-17) of the National Building Research Institute bill [621/2025]; a presented Bill version is not in the evidence, and §20 on public-service officers does not address this option.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded for any year of assessment **"prior to April 1, 2018"** [013/2026 §37].

- The new section 202(2A)(a) applies this "notwithstanding that any un- deducted balance of such deduction under the repealed Act remains as at April 1, 2018" [013/2026 §37].
- Note the contrast: the exclusion in paragraphs (b) and (c) of the same subsection instead covers years of assessment "commencing on or after April 1, 2018" [013/2026 §37].
- Evidence is from the Inland Revenue (Amendment) bill published as a Gazette supplement on 2026-02-24, whose text is stated to be identical in 022/2026 [013/2026 §37].

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Two different terms apply in the 2025 bill: a moneylending licence under sections 23/24 is "valid for a period of one year" [645/2025 §25(c)], while a licence to carry on the microfinance business is "issued for a period of three years" [645/2025 §32(7)].

- Section 32(9) applies section 25 to microfinance licences but omits paragraph (c), so the one-year rule does not override the three-year term [645/2025 §32(9)].
- Both terms run with conditions and an annual licence fee, and the licence must "specify the date of expiry" and be "non transferable" [645/2025 §25].
- An older and differently titled bill, the Microfinance (GS) bill of 2015, instead ran a licence to "the thirty-first day of December next following" [080/2015 §5].

Caveats: section 32(9) is truncated in the extract ("shall mutatis mutandis ap"), and drafts 645/2025 and 653/2025 are noted as identical; committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Notice of dishonour may be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means which sufficiently identify the bill, and intimate that the bill has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment" [601/2025 §8].

- This substitutes s.49(5) of the principal Ordinance [601/2025 §8]; the text is identical in Bill 612/2025 [612/2025 §8].

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
The only passage labelled as the Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) Bill defines a "qualified auditor" as either an individual, or a firm of accountants whose resident partners, are members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute established by law) and hold a certificate to practice issued by that Institute's Council [626/2025 §11].

- Individual: "a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or any other Institute established by law" holding "a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute" [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].
- Firm: "a firm of Accountants each of the resident partners" of which meets the same membership and certificate requirement [626/2025 §11(4)(b)].
- The audit itself is by an auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].

Caveats: This clause is standard boilerplate repeated across foundation bills (e.g. [547/2024 §11], [223/2022 §10]); the text as given may not be the bill's own verified wording.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society (as "body corporate") may take and hold any movable or immovable property vesting in it by "purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise", holding it for the purposes of the Act and its rules, "with power to sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same" [047/2026 §13].

- It may "purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings" needed for its purposes and "deal with or dispose of the same as determined by the Council" [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may "undertake, accept, execute, perform and administer any lawful trust" with similar objects, or any real or personal property, to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)].
- Management of its property is governed by rules made under section 7, on "the administration and management of the property of the body corporate" [047/2026 §7(1)(f)].

Caveats: This is the Bill of 2026-06-25; the GS version of 2026-06-11 (§§6, 13) is worded identically in these passages.

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the substituted section 35, employees of businesses licensed **before** commencement get a three-year income-tax exemption, while employees of businesses licensed **on or after** commencement are liable to income tax [654/2025 §3].

- Pre-commencement licensees: "for a period of three years" from the month after commencement, a resident employee's employment income is "exempt from income tax" and treated as a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account; a non-resident's employment income is exempt and they are not liable on income earned outside Sri Lanka [654/2025 §3].
- Post-commencement licensees: "Any employment income of a resident employee and a non-resident employee ... shall be liable to income tax" [654/2025 §3].

Caveats: This is the Bill version (2025-12-05); the GS version [652/2025 §3] has identical text. Both renderings contain garbled cross-references to section 27 of Act No. 11 of 2021.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The bill amends the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005 by replacing wording in the sections listed in a Schedule, plus targeted amendments to particular sections. [018/2026 §2]

- Section 16A: repeals the "finance business" definition, replaces "funds or property" with "funds, property or other assets", and inserts definitions including "foreign terrorist fighter" and "armed conflict". [018/2026 §16]
- Section 3: new proviso that funds need not be "actually used" or linked to a specific act, plus new modes of liability (organizing, accomplice, contribution) and a new offence in subsection (2B). [018/2026 §4]
- Section 2A(2): extended application to acts wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka directed at Sri Lanka, citizens or government facilities. [018/2026 §3]

Caveats: Text identical in 029/2026; the Schedule's substituted words are not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?

The maximum is **one year**: the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member," "warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill (Bill 004/2026, 2026-01-20), a person qualifies as an "occupant" if they are in lawful occupation and have had "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises "for a period of more than three months" before the events covered by sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The same three-month threshold appears in the earlier Gazette version (GS 634/2025, 2025-09-18) [634/2025 §2].
- Both conditions must be met: lawful occupation and the three-month period of undisturbed, uninterrupted occupation [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: Neither version states a precise day count; the text says "more than three months."

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
The Gambling Regulatory Authority Bill disqualifies a person "over seventy years of age" from appointment as a member of the Board [613/2025 §9(i)]. The same clause appears verbatim in the Gazette version [594/2025 §9(i)] (GS, 2025-05-27; Bill, 2025-06-17), so the two versions do not differ.

- The limit is framed as a disqualification "from being appointed", not as a rule on continuing to serve past 70 [613/2025 §9].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?

The longest jail term is **one year** under the proposed replacement of section 27 of the Financial Transactions Reporting Act. [021/2026 §31]

- The offence is arriving in or leaving Sri Lanka with cash or bearer negotiable instruments exceeding the Minister-specified sum without reporting it. [021/2026 §31]
- On Magistrate conviction, the penalty is a fine up to three times the value **or** “imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year,” or both. [021/2026 §31]

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the Sri Lanka Cricket bill, the penalty is a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)] (identical text in 077/2026).

- The subscription itself is due "on or before the thirty first day of December" of the preceding year [072/2026 §30(3)]; the doubled fee is payable by "the thirtieth day of April of the following year" [072/2026 §30(4)].
- Non-payment by that later date means automatic forfeiture of voting rights [072/2026 §30(5)], and removal from the Register of Members if unpaid for six months after the due date [072/2026 §30(6)].

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (Bill, 2026-10-06), the magistrate must, "without giving any advance notice", visit the approved place of detention "once a month", interview suspects, and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other documents [078/2026 §33(1)].

- On observing or being told of torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, he "shall forthwith" order the suspect be produced for examination by a Judicial Medical Officer, with the report submitted to him [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, he acts under section 31 [078/2026 §33(5)].

Caveats: The older, differently titled Anti Terrorism Bill [444/2024 §32] provides a weekly visit and covers only the suspect's own place of detention; it is not the same Bill.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
The **Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment)** bill, 576/2025 — a Gazette version published 2025-03-28, with identical text also in 579/2025 — amends the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979.

- It inserts new "sections 144A and 144B" into the 1979 Act, allowing a Magistrate to "dispense with the personal attendance in court of a suspect or an accused" on specified grounds [576/2025 §2].
- It amends the Second Schedule by inserting new Forms 24 and 25 covering requests to serve a commission abroad and the commissioner's oath/affirmation [576/2025 §6].

Note: the Gambling Regulatory Authority bill (613/2025) also references the 1979 Code but only applies it "mutatis mutandis"; it does not amend it [613/2025 §57].

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** — Bill No. **065/2026**, presented 18 August 2026 (a Gazette version, **057/2026**, was published 7 August 2026).

- It raises the Supreme Court retirement age to "sixty-seven years" and Court of Appeal to "sixty-five years", with the Chief Justice retiring at 67 or after six years in that office, whichever is earlier [065/2026 §2].
- It amends Article 137 to allow "not more than twenty four other Judges" (up from nineteen) [065/2026 §3].
- Short title: "This Act may be cited as the Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution" [057/2026 §1].

Caveats: An identically titled 2024 bill exists ([460/2024 §2]) but amends different provisions — the 2026 bill is the one matching your description. I have no text beyond these clauses.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Rent (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20) — note its title is "Rent (Repeal)", not "Tenancy" — provides that "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].

- Repeal does not take immediate effect for tenants: no ejectment action for "a period of one year from the relevant date" [006/2026 §3(a)], and no rent above the authorised rent may be demanded or received for that year [006/2026 §3(b)].
- Pending Rent Board and Board of Review proceedings must be concluded "within a period of one year from the relevant date" [006/2026 §3(d)–(e)].

Caveats: The evidence names the statute "Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972"; no bill titled "Tenancy Act" appears, and the "relevant date" is not defined in the passages given.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)** bill — a Gazette version (GS) published **6 February 2026** — constitutes the body corporate [011/2026 §2]. Note the same text also appears in 015/2026.

- It is incorporated "with perpetual succession" under the name "Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children", with power to sue and be sued and a common seal [011/2026 §2(1)].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [011/2026 §2(2)].
- Objects include conducting educational and skills programmes and establishing an IT training centre, without distinction based on race, religion, language, caste, gender, political opinion or place of birth [011/2026 §3].

Caveats: The title in the heading ("Education Centre for Children") differs slightly from the incorporated name in §2(1) ("Centre for Education for Children"); only the GS version is in evidence, not a presented Bill.
